title: Permission matrix separates administration from financial authority
context: Research into enterprise treasury tools (Treasury Systems, Nomentia, TIS) shows a consistent pattern: 'managing access' (add/remove users, grant roles) is separated from 'financial authority' (propose / approve / book / override). Treasury Systems explicitly recommends removing its unrestricted 'Everything' role after implementation. Nomentia and TIS gate by specific business action, not role name. Our previous Admin gate was role-based (`require_role('ADMIN')`) — good for the initial cut but limiting.
decision: Introduce a Permission enum and a role→permissions matrix as the single source of truth for authority. Roles remain the grant unit; permissions are the gate unit. Backend endpoints use `require_permission(...)` in place of / alongside `require_role(...)`. The Admin page renders effective access in plain English ('Can propose deposits · Cannot approve · Cannot change policy') derived from the matrix.
invariants: ADMIN does NOT grant automatic dealing or approval authority — administration is a separate concern from financial authority. Treasury Systems and Nomentia both enforce this shape.
COMPLIANCE_OFFICER is read-only across the audit trail; never mutates the book.
Every backend gate uses a permission, not a role name. Roles are the grant unit; permissions are the enforcement unit.
The plain-English label per permission is authoritative — the Admin UI reads it verbatim so 'Can' / 'Cannot' phrasing stays consistent across screens.
consequences: backend/app/services/permissions.py holds the Permission enum, ROLE_PERMISSIONS, PERMISSION_LABEL and summarise_permissions()
backend/app/api/deps.py — require_permission() dependency factory (require_role kept for legacy)
GET /admin/roles now returns each role's permission list + plain-English can[]
GET /admin/users now returns each user's effective_access { held, can, cannot }
GET /auth/me + POST /auth/token now return the caller's permissions[] alongside roles[] — the frontend prefers permissions for gating UI
frontend/lib/session.ts — can(...permissions) helper; hasRole kept for coarse persona-nav gating
frontend/app/admin/page.tsx — RolesCard shows 'Can …' per role; UsersTable shows an EffectiveAccessSummary per user; EditUserPanel shows a RoleChangePreview of gains/losses before Save
future_work: New backend endpoints should default to require_permission over require_role.
Company/legal-entity scope (Phase B) will layer onto Permission by pairing (permission, entity_id).
Four-eye control (Phase D) applies to grants of ADMIN / CFO / COMPLIANCE_OFFICER — grants of permissions that would elevate financial or administrative authority.
